speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to Dr. Agent's clinic. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; to begin my assessment, please describe exactly where the pain is located and how it started. Additionally, have you noticed any swelling, deformity, or inability to grip objects?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain radiating to your elbow and worsening when holding your infant suggests possible De Quervain's tenosynovitis or early CARS, potentially exacerbated by your past fall. Given your mother's history of autoimmune joint pain treated with methotrexate, we must rule out an inflammatory component. Please describe exactly how much pain you feel when I ask you to make a fist and then tilt your hand toward your little finger, and do you see any swelling at the base of your thumb?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis. Based on the pain location (right thumb/wrist), aggravation by lifting an infant, and response to ice, your symptoms are most consistent with inflammation of the tendons on the thumb side of your wrist. The past fall and family history suggest we should also consider an inflammatory component, but the physical presentation points strongly to this specific tendon issue.
